purpose: Authoritative-vendor industrial data-platform delta. Promotes Litmus Edge from discovery-queued to spec-verified and adds Cybus Connectware and N3uron as spec-verified industrial connectivity targets. All reuse existing protocol profiles behind the customer edge. No sandbox or tenant credentials were used; writes, management-plane operations, remote provisioning, industrial control and agent actions remain disabled.

patch.evidenceNote: Litmus' current 4.0.x API portal documents REST and GraphQL APIs for DeviceHub, Digital Twins, DataHub, Analytics, Integrations, OPC UA and System, with OAuth2 client-credentials or API-token authentication. It also documents materially different 3.16.x endpoints. Litmus Edge and Edge Manager contain device, application, integration, backup, certificate and fleet-management operations, so Manufacturing WFM restricts this connector to approved data-plane read/query/subscribe surfaces and treats management APIs as a separate authority. No Litmus environment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: customer-approved Litmus identity restricted to minimum data-plane read/query resources
MQTT subscribe-only topics and OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe only with authenticated encrypted sessions
no device/tag writes, flows or analytics mutation, application deployment, integration creation, backups, certificates, users or Edge Manager fleet control
dataAvailableOrExpected: device, driver, tag and asset discovery metadata
near-real-time industrial tag values, source timestamps and local time-series data
Digital Twin hierarchy and contextual asset relationships where configured
normalized telemetry exposed through MQTT or OPC UA
automationOpportunities: adjust staffing demand and redeployment recommendations from actual machine/line state
reuse device and Digital Twin hierarchy to accelerate site and work-centre mapping
forecast recovery, paid-idle and overtime risk from machine availability patterns
coordinate maintenance and specialist staffing from operational context
reuse an existing edge abstraction rather than build duplicate direct PLC integrations
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle labour during sustained line unavailability
reduce overtime by aligning labour with actual recovery state
reduce mapping effort by reusing device and Digital Twin hierarchy
reduce duplicate telemetry infrastructure at multi-site customers
dataGaps: worker, payroll, absence, skill and roster truth normally remains outside Litmus
device/tag names and Digital Twin models are customer-specific
API and authentication differ between 4.0.x and 3.16.x
derived analytics must be distinguished from raw observations
Edge Manager bridge availability and permissions vary by deployment
constraintsRisks: Litmus Edge is plant/on-prem infrastructure and remains behind the customer edge
data and powerful management APIs coexist, so a usable token is not automatically least privilege
MQTT and OPC UA require authenticated encrypted production sessions
schema/version changes require fingerprints and remapping
buffered/replayed data must retain source time and replay age
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse REST, GraphQL, MQTT and OPC UA profiles for a thin Litmus adapter with 4.0.x/3.16.x capability discovery, operation allowlists, token rotation, topic/node mappings, freshness/quality handling and hierarchy fingerprints. Keep fixtures read/query/subscribe-only until an authorised Litmus lab or customer edge can prove least-privilege authentication and read round-trip.

systems.name: Cybus Connectware
systems.evidenceNote: Cybus documentation describes Connectware as an industrial integration platform with REST APIs, an internal MQTT broker and an OPC UA server. HTTP and MQTT permissions distinguish read from write; MQTT supports username/password or x.509 mTLS; production OPC UA guidance recommends SignAndEncrypt with named Connectware credentials. Because the same platform can commission services, publish data and expose bidirectional servers, Manufacturing WFM uses only approved REST reads, MQTT subscriptions and OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe. No Connectware environment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated role with HTTP read permissions only for approved endpoints
MQTT read/subscribe permission only for approved topic prefixes, preferably with x.509 mTLS
OPC UA named user restricted to approved nodes with SignAndEncrypt and certificate validation
no service commissioning, user/role administration, MQTT publish, OPC UA write/method or other control-plane authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: normalized MQTT topics representing machine, line, sensor and application data
OPC UA nodes and hierarchy exposed by customer commissioning files
approved REST status, service and metadata resources
timestamps and values routed from connected OT and IT sources
resource metadata useful for site, line and endpoint mapping
automationOpportunities: reuse Connectware's normalized OT/IT data layer instead of individual direct PLC integrations
refresh labour demand and redeployment recommendations from live machine state
correlate labour, downtime, throughput and energy across heterogeneous equipment
accelerate multi-site implementation from service/resource metadata
use persistent-session/reconnect data only with replay-age freshness controls
savingsHypotheses: reduce machine-specific connector engineering by consuming one governed data projection
reduce paid idle time and overtime by matching staffing to actual machine availability
reduce implementation/support cost through reusable topic and commissioning mappings
reduce reconciliation effort using normalized MQTT/OPC UA representations
reduce cloud exposure to low-level plant protocols
dataGaps: topic hierarchy, commissioning files, nodes and resource IDs are customer-defined
module and server availability differs by deployment
management APIs require endpoint-level least privilege
source quality remains dependent on the connected OT/IT source
constraintsRisks: Connectware remains inside the customer/site edge boundary
HTTP and MQTT permissions must not use broad wildcard write grants
persistent MQTT sessions can replay a burst after outages
major versions can change topic or commissioning behaviour
REST/MQTT/OPC UA surfaces are bidirectional-capable and require technical read-only enforcement
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse REST, MQTT and OPC UA profiles for a thin Connectware adapter with version discovery, read endpoint allowlists, role/permission checks, topic ACL verification, OPC UA SignAndEncrypt/certificate validation, replay-age watermarks and commissioning/topic schema fingerprints. Obtain an authorised Connectware test deployment before promoting beyond spec verification.

systems.name: N3uron Industrial IoT & DataOps Platform
systems.evidenceNote: N3uron's current documentation describes REST API Server, MQTT/Sparkplug, OPC UA Server, Historian and a broad set of industrial clients. Its REST API can retrieve data but can also transmit commands; security guidance supports HTTPS, role/token access control and TagFilters. Sparkplug supports store-and-forward, and OPC UA exposes history plus methods. Manufacturing WFM therefore consumes only approved read/query/subscribe data and separately gates REST commands, MQTT publishing, OPC UA methods/writes, configuration and agent actions. No N3uron environment was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated API identity/token restricted by role and TagFilters to required paths and reads
MQTT/Sparkplug subscribe-only over TLS, preferably certificate-authenticated
OPC UA Browse/Read/Subscribe/history only using named identity and approved nodes
no REST commands/configuration, tag writes, MQTT publish, OPC UA methods/writes, scripting or agent actions
dataAvailableOrExpected: real-time and historical industrial tags through the N3uron data model
raw and contextual values collected from OPC UA, Modbus, MQTT, Siemens and other plant sources
historian, aggregated and derived tags where configured
MQTT/Sparkplug streams with source timestamps and store-and-forward behaviour
OPC UA hierarchy/history and approved platform health data
automationOpportunities: reuse N3uron as an abstraction across legacy and modern plant protocols
drive staffing demand and redeployment from actual machine and line state
combine historian and live state to forecast recovery, specialist demand and overtime risk
use contextual tags to improve work-centre mapping and labour-to-output attribution
correlate utility/energy telemetry with staffing and production where exposed
savingsHypotheses: reduce bespoke machine connector development through a normalized data model
reduce idle and overtime cost by tying workforce decisions to production-state evidence
reduce data-loss/reconciliation effort with local historian/store-and-forward while preserving freshness
reduce multi-site implementation effort through reusable tag/templates
reduce cloud access to low-level plant protocols
dataGaps: worker/payroll/absence/skills truth normally remains outside N3uron
tag paths, templates, derived tags and modules are customer-specific
derived/aggregated data must be marked separately from raw observations
southbound source quality and semantics vary by device/protocol
REST/API and agent surfaces may expose actions beyond WFM data needs
constraintsRisks: N3uron remains an edge/plant platform behind customer-controlled routing
REST is bidirectional and can transmit commands, requiring operation-level read enforcement
Sparkplug store-and-forward can backfill old values after outages
OPC UA can expose methods and multiple security modes; production requires authenticated encrypted sessions and no method calls
TagFilters, role permissions, certificates and version/module fingerprints must be verified per site
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse REST, MQTT/Sparkplug and OPC UA profiles for a thin N3uron adapter with module/version discovery, TagFilter-aware mapping, read-operation allowlists, TLS/certificate validation, Sparkplug birth/death and replay handling, source/ingestion timestamps and raw-versus-derived provenance. Obtain an authorised N3uron node before promoting beyond spec verification.
